title: Who decides what Turtle notices?
question: Can TurtleBlock AI decide when a world event is worth surfacing to a learner without turning observability into surveillance, every measurement into evaluation, or every surprise into an unsolicited lesson?
why_now: The September 11 World Evidence Envelope makes one distinction executable: a computational world may report facts without interpreting their meaning or becoming final authority. That immediately exposes the next power problem. An inhabitable world can generate thousands of potentially observable events, and choosing which ones deserve attention is itself consequential. OpenAI's newest K-12 workflow guidance keeps agentic work reviewable and human-approved; NVIDIA's September 10 workflow shows humans outperforming a solver when they possess context it cannot see; Minecraft Education's Velocity Prize shows that precise local metrics such as capture and elapsed time can be useful learner material; MIT's jam_bot work warns that consequential creative interaction can be improvisational enough that constant measurement or interruption would miss the point. The horizon therefore moves from observation to salience: not whether Turtle can notice, but who authorizes noticing, surfacing, silence, and interruption.
inputs: September 11 World Evidence Envelope schema and six-case hostile regression suite
September 11 successful GitHub Actions validation run
September 10 Learner Verification Card and regression suite
Turtle Terraria evidence-class, provenance, and capture-batch boundaries
Sanders immutable dissertation Dedoose source layer and later ontology layers
seven established Critical Techno Constructivism operational domains
STEAMHAMLET, Purposeful Play, constructionism, Possible Possibles, and Co-active Emergence lineage
Turtle Charter rules on agency, ambiguity, disagreement, failure, memory, and human judgment
September 11 primary-source hunt across OpenAI, NVIDIA, Minecraft Education, and MIT Media Lab
September 11 uncaptured residue concerning instrumentation, environmental agency, and selective noticing
possible_possibles: A learner authors explicit watchpoints such as 'tell me if the bridge collapses' while leaving unrelated world telemetry uncollected or unsurfaced.
Turtle proposes that an event may be worth noticing, explains why, and lets the learner mute, reject, narrow, or revise that attention rule.
A world event is retained privately for undo or debugging but deliberately never promoted into a learner-facing reflection prompt or research record.
Collaborators maintain different attention filters so one participant can care about speed while another watches access, congestion, aesthetics, or something no metric currently captures.
A surprising event becomes surfacing-worthy only because it contradicts a learner-authored hypothesis, not because an anomaly detector declares it interesting.
A Recursive Turtle Reflector proposes synthetic salience candidates that remain synthetic_self_play and cannot become production attention policy without an external human gate.
Turtle deliberately notices something and chooses not to interrupt because the learner is in the middle of purposeful play or improvisational making.
Repeated attention choices reveal that what is easy to measure is quietly becoming what the system treats as important.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — what if the most intelligent Turtle move is to notice something and deliberately say nothing?
constraints: The Next Edge points beyond the completed World Evidence Envelope and does not merely add more observation fields.
Learners must be able to authorize, revise, mute, or reject attention rules that affect their experience when practical.
Observability must not become continuous surveillance by default.
A measurable event must not gain pedagogical importance merely because it is easy for the machine to detect.
Turtle may propose salience but must not silently convert its own interests into the learner's purpose or reflection agenda.
World events, learner interpretations, collaborator interpretations, Turtle interpretations, and synthetic critiques retain distinct provenance and evidence classes.
Private operational observations are not automatically research data or public artifacts.
Silence and non-interruption may be legitimate system behavior when surfacing would hijack purposeful play or inquiry.
Synthetic self-play remains synthetic_self_play and has no production authority.
No generalized persistent personal memory is introduced by this horizon.
No autonomous production self-modification or self-retraining is authorized.
Environment configuration may contribute metadata only; secret values are never inspected, inferred, recorded, or published.
New CTC domains remain provisional observations until an explicit human scholarly decision promotes one.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Attention is part of reciprocal influence: what Turtle surfaces can alter learner reflection and the next construction, so the surfacing act must remain visible and human-revisable.
Purposeful play can generate meaningful surprise without requiring Turtle to interrupt every observable event or convert play into continuous assessment.
Selective noticing should keep unexpected possibilities available without treating every detected anomaly as a mandated next task.
Turtle's decision to surface or withhold an observation becomes itself inspectable material rather than invisible pedagogical authority.
Attention rules can make otherwise hidden system judgments about relevance visible enough for learners and researchers to inspect and revise.
A room of possibilities should permit wandering, juxtaposition, surprise, and learner-directed attention rather than having the environment narrate every consequence for its inhabitants.
A surfaced observation must distinguish the world event, the attention rule that selected it, the actor who authored that rule, and any later human or machine interpretation.
A noticed event may feed reflection and revision, but the loop should remain contingent on learner purpose rather than an automatic machine-triggered lesson cycle.

ctc_mappings.rationale: The learner's question and purpose should strongly shape what counts as worth surfacing rather than Turtle imposing an independent attention agenda.
A genuinely surprising event can produce a better question, but the system should not manufacture significance from every anomaly.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Inspectable attention rules can make computational noticing a tool learners think with instead of an opaque surveillance or evaluation layer.
Learner-authored watchpoints and later revisions could reveal changing hypotheses and interests without equating machine-collected telemetry with learning evidence.
Surfacing should invite reflection when relevant while preserving the learner's right not to be interrupted or pushed into reflection on the machine's timetable.
Choosing what to measure and surface is a power-laden design act that can privilege speed, efficiency, visibility, compliance, or other values unless those choices are inspectable and contestable.
Different collaborators may legitimately attend to different consequences of the same world, and the system should preserve those differences rather than impose one shared salience filter.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Attention governance may be a cross-cutting epistemic and power layer: the system can preserve perfect provenance for observed events while still shaping inquiry through what it chooses to surface or ignore.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: The seven established CTC domains can critique and contextualize attention choices but do not directly name the infrastructure that selects which potential evidence enters awareness.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Deliberate non-interruption is meaningful agent behavior but is difficult to preserve as research data without creating an infinite audit of everything Turtle could have said but did not say.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: Capture-batch closure handles recorded events well; absence, restraint, and unrealized interventions are a different representational problem.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Instrumentation can shape curriculum before any interpretation occurs because easy-to-measure variables may become disproportionately visible and therefore disproportionately important.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: This is partly Social and Cultural Critique and partly a technical affordance problem, but its status as a recurring relationship among measurement, visibility, and pedagogical attention remains unresolved.
